## Repeatable ghost commissioning before held-out native validation

Effective 2026-08-25, an end-to-end **ghost** is the default commissioning
lane before a finite held-out native attempt. A ghost is explicitly
**development work**. It is repeatable, may use declared development,
calibration, or training seeds, and may drive implementation or controller
changes. It never becomes a positive, negative, equivalence, release, or score
result, even when every gate passes.

A route ghost answers one narrow question: can the intended production path
construct a native world, take the code-path-relevant real physics steps,
finalize, retain and publish its artifacts, propagate a complete terminal,
and receive an execution-valid classification? A ghost passes when that route
works. It does **not** need to walk, turn, recover, or pass an official physical
threshold. A complete valid physics negative is a successful route ghost; an
infrastructure-invalid or incomplete result is not.

A ghost must use the actual production implementation: production entry
point, native worker, canonical policy and profile loader, engine adapter,
world construction, control step, recorder, finalization, evaluator code,
CAS publication, terminal propagation, and supervisor assembly. Its declared
development contract may use the smallest schedule, horizon, seed, and cell
set adequate to exercise the named route risks. The permitted differences
from the later official run are explicit:

- `authority_mode` is `development_ghost`, never official evidence;
- one seed is drawn from the declared development partition by default;
- the output root and attempt identity are ghost-specific; and
- a `coverage_manifest` declares the cells, phases, steps, finalization paths,
  and infrastructure risks the shortened development route actually covers.

A shortened ghost schedule must be supplied through the same parameterized
production scheduling and count-projection path and must still reach real
finalization. It may not bypass a phase it claims to commission. There may be
no ghost-only physics implementation, synthetic substitute for a native
worker, permissive infrastructure handling, alternate retention path, or
hand-built terminal. The production evaluator may consume an explicit
development-ghost contract so it does not demand official behavior thresholds,
but it must retain the same identity, completeness, and infrastructure checks
and must report the observed physics outcome without promoting it.

Coverage, not duration, determines adequacy. A minimal turning route ghost may
need only enough real steps to construct each advertised native engine, apply
the relevant command-arm paths, write at least one real trace record, end the
short declared horizon, publish through CAS, assemble the terminal set, and
invoke the evaluator. One or two real steps can be adequate when they cover
the named risk. A longer or full-horizon ghost is required only when an
explicit risk appears late or at volume—for example buffer growth, timeout,
late phase transition, full-trace retention, terminal restoration, or final
matrix aggregation. Multiple seeds are required only when seed, morphology,
or fixture selection changes a code path being commissioned. Seed repetition
for behavioral confidence belongs to the later physical evidence design, not
the route ghost.

A test of a proxy route remains a component test, not an end-to-end ghost. A
long development world used to tune or observe locomotion is a development
rehearsal, not a stronger ghost and not held-out validation. The future
official seed, cohort, or world may not be previewed, debugged, or replayed as
either kind of development work.

Every ghost outcome—positive, negative, rejected, invalid, or incomplete—is
retained append-only with source, dependency, toolchain, environment, seed,
cohort, route, and output provenance. Compact content-addressed retention is
preferred, but compaction may not discard a result or blur its authority mode.
Ghost evidence may guide the next development design; it may not be relabeled
as held-out evidence or pooled into the finite official population.

After the last route-affecting source, controller, configuration, evaluator,
or orchestration change, the default readiness floor is:

1. focused component checks for the changed seam;
2. one smallest coverage-adequate route ghost using one development seed by
   default, repeated after a route repair until it produces a complete
   execution-valid result;
3. an additional targeted or full-horizon ghost only when the coverage
   manifest identifies a distinct unexercised code risk; then
4. an exact source/toolchain/environment freeze, complete zero-world gates and
   negative controls, separate adoption, and one fresh held-out native run.

There is no automatic second seed and no automatic full-matrix or full-horizon
ghost. Any load-bearing route change after the passing ghost requires a fresh
coverage review and rerun of the affected route. Thresholds, margins, cohort
definitions, and population claims must still state their provenance and
adequacy before the held-out freeze. Development tuning must stop before that
freeze.

Targeted canaries remain valuable for stable semantic invariants, dangerous
regressions, and negative controls. However, discovering an integration bug
does not automatically require adding one bespoke campaign canary to every
future critical path. Record the incident, add a focused regression when its
cost and diagnostic value justify it, and prove the whole production route in
ghost commissioning. Canaries complement the ghost; neither substitutes for
the complete zero-world gate or held-out native validation.

New records use a `ledger_scope` containing `subsystem`, `engine_scope`,
`authority_mode`, and `question_class`. Typical labels are
`[turning/rapier]`, `[turning/3e]`, `[recovery/core]`, and
`[harness/3e]`. A turning ghost is development work; the frozen nine-cell
turning question is a finite decision; a complete route-parity proof may be
equivalence/non-inferiority work only when its complete population and zero or
declared margins are justified. These classes must not be conflated.

### Qualification economy and audit-growth control

Effective 2026-08-28, a new successor identity does not by itself justify a
new executable audit. The default successor contribution is a declarative
contract or manifest consumed by shared qualification, mutation, role,
retention, and evaluation machinery. Campaign-specific executable audit code
is exceptional and must correspond to a genuinely new public contract, ABI,
physical observable or invariant, engine transport, evidence/dependency shape,
previously untestable failure class, evaluator semantic, or release claim.

Qualification work has three separate lanes:

1. The development lane uses focused subsystem tests, repeatable non-authority
   development runs, and the smallest adequate ghost. A surface ghost loads
   and instantiates the real production entry point, completes one valid
   handshake, and proves one deliberate typed refusal with zero worlds. A
   native-route ghost may construct one minimal native model and take one or
   two real solver steps only when construction or stepping is the changed
   integration surface. A longer horizon, additional seed, or larger cell
   population requires a named late- or volume-dependent code risk.
2. The physical-qualification lane uses the commissioned shared authorization
   kernel, the exact active lineage, and the worker/evaluator/supervisor role
   controls. The normal shape remains 12 shared gates plus the smallest exact
   active lineage and three role gates. Additional gates require a named new
   safeguard or capability; reassurance alone is not adequate provenance.
3. The historical-regression lane owns complete cold re-execution of retained
   audits. It runs at least once per seven active development days, after a
   material change to the shared authorization kernel, evidence machinery,
   ABI/schema registry, audit executor, or core adapter interface, and for each
   SDK release candidate. Its latest accepted result is a content-addressed
   receipt binding the exact source, audit population, dependencies,
   toolchain, environment, start/end times, and per-audit outcomes. An
   unrelated historical failure remains real maintenance debt, but it blocks
   an active physical campaign only when dependency-impact analysis connects
   it to that campaign or to a shared safeguard the campaign requires.

An ordinary coding defect belongs in the smallest shared subsystem regression
that owns it. A shared schema or ABI defect belongs in shared versioning/core
conformance; an adapter-wide defect belongs in shared adapter conformance; a
campaign-specific frozen criterion belongs in declarative campaign data; a
possibly disconnected route belongs in a development ghost. A typo, new seed,
new campaign number, or generalized anxiety is not sufficient reason to add a
permanent campaign canary.

The following are engineering review triggers, not scientific thresholds and
not reasons to rewrite an observed result:

- more than one new campaign-specific executable audit file, or roughly more
  than 150 nonblank lines of campaign-specific audit logic, requires an
  explicit explanation of the new contract and why shared machinery cannot
  express it;
- before a third copy of the same assertion pattern appears, the common
  mechanism must be parameterized or extracted;
- unexplained scoped-gate growth, or more than 25 percent duration growth over
  the previous comparable qualification after accounting for build/cache
  state, requires profiling before more gates are added; and
- a proposed full-horizon or multi-seed ghost must identify the exact risk
  that one handshake, one typed refusal, or one to two native steps cannot
  cover.

These rules are enforced through design review and existing receipts. Do not
create a new bootstrap, meta-ledger, or executable audit whose sole purpose is
to police audit size. Preserve existing audits and observed campaigns exactly;
reuse or extract their mechanics prospectively when a second real consumer
appears, and remove duplication before a third copy is authored.

Whenever Cole explicitly resumes hashed scientific work, this policy governs
successor development. It does not itself resume paused work, authorize a
physical claim, or change the score.

superiority, equivalence/non-inferiority, repeatability, robustness, or
population study. The adequacy argument is correspondingly finite: observing
every declared cell can answer whether this exact SDK1 profile and fixture
passes in all three named bindings, but it cannot estimate a broader success

## Consumed R23D71 finite-decision contract

R23D71 was a physical **finite decision** on unused seed `23191`. The initial
qualification's provenance failure remains a retained zero-world process
negative. A distinct corrected clean-pushed source passed `16/16` gates on the
commissioned runtime, was separately adopted, and passed the complete `9/9`
authorization population. Exactly nine genuine worlds then ran serially. Every
worker completed `2,992` controller steps and retained a full CAS trace.

The frozen evaluator returned
`invalid_or_incomplete_exact_seed_23191_three_engine_portable_turning`. For the
six directly evaluated Godot/Jolt and Rapier reports,
`R23D65_TRACE_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY` records a receipt-contract failure: trace bytes
and row counts were retained, but `trace_artifact` lacked required embedded
transport fields. The three MuJoCo worker reports additionally omitted
`question_class`, so the supervisor retained them as transport failures before
the evaluator could apply their behavior gates. The evaluator also recorded
`R23D34_FORWARD_DISPLACEMENT` for every Rapier cell against the prospectively
declared `0.030123046875 m` threshold. That is a real physical-gate observation,
but the invalid matrix supplies neither a valid finite positive nor a valid
finite negative.

The [immutable closure](../sdk/turning/r23d71_success_terminal_projection_repaired_three_engine_turning_validation_closure_v1.json)
and [audit](../tests/test_qsdk_r23d71_physical_closure.ps1) preserve the exact
72-file, 677,221,819-byte population, all nine traces, and every non-claim.
R23D71 is consumed; no same-identity or selective rerun is permitted. The
earlier adequacy argument for a purely synthetic success payload is rejected by
this observation: it did not cover real receipt assembly. The successor method
is complete zero-world conformance followed by a bounded **development** smoke
through each native producer and evaluator, using no held-out claim and only
enough steps to prove the transport. Rapier behavior work is a distinct
development question before any new finite decision. Turning, equivalence,
robustness, prone-to-standing, and release claims remain false at `10/25`.

## Retained R23D71 measurement-origin development diagnosis

The bounded [diagnosis](../sdk/turning/r23d71_forward_displacement_measurement_origin_diagnosis_v1.json)
is **development**, not a finite decision, superiority test, or
equivalence/non-inferiority test. It reads the complete nine-trace R23D71
engine-arm population, verifies every trace against the immutable closure, and
runs the unchanged cycle-integrated measurement from a pinned Git blob. The
[audit](../sdk/audit_r23d71_forward_displacement_measurement_origin_diagnosis.ps1)
rejects eight mutations and opens zero worlds.

The observation isolates two separate causes. Rapier's near-zero historical
